scenarios.title: {J}'s First Own Place
text: For the first time, {J} can afford his own apartment. The estate agent shows him three: a tiny studio near the training ground, a two-bed in a new tower, and a penthouse he definitely can't afford.
{MUM} wants him to keep living in club housing. {J} wants his own front door.

choices.label: The tiny studio
choices.text: It's small enough to touch both walls. He sleeps ten minutes from training and saves money every month.

choices.label: The two-bed in the tower
choices.text: A spare room means {BFf} visits, and {MUM} visits, and once both at the same time, which was chaos.

choices.label: The penthouse
choices.text: The view is unreal. So is the rent. The squad nickname him 'the landlord'. A gossip account posts the building.

scenarios.title: The Watch
text: Every senior player in the dressing room wears a watch that costs more than {J}'s parents' house. {T} shows him a catalogue. 'You've made it. Act like it.'
A luxury watch brand invites {J} to a private showroom. The glass of water they offer him is in crystal.

choices.label: Buy it
choices.text: It's beautiful. He checks the time constantly for a week. {DAD} sees it on TV and says nothing, which says a lot.

choices.label: Buy one for {DAD} instead
choices.text: {DAD} unwraps it, says 'too much', and wears it to every family gathering for the rest of his life.

choices.label: No thanks
choices.text: His plastic sports watch becomes a dressing-room joke and then, slowly, a kind of badge of honour.

scenarios.title: A New Way of Eating
text: A famous veteran swears his career was extended five years by a strict new diet: no sugar, no fried food, everything weighed. He offers to share his chef.
The club nutritionist has a new plan for {J}. It involves a lot of fish. {J} has never knowingly enjoyed a fish.

choices.label: Go all in
choices.text: Three weeks in, he's sharper in sprints and quieter at dinner parties. His family visits and finds nothing in his fridge but broccoli.

choices.label: 80% of the time
choices.text: Fish on weekdays, {FOOD} on Sundays. The nutritionist sighs but accepts it.

choices.label: Politely ignore it
choices.hint: Happy now. Maybe not at thirty.
choices.text: He keeps eating what he likes. The nutritionist writes something in a file.

scenarios.title: The Club Promoter
text: A nightclub promoter offers {J} a free VIP table every weekend 'for being seen'. He's done the same for half the league. Some of them have stopped being seen in matches.
The hottest club in the city wants {J} at their opening night. There will be celebrities, photographers and a very long night.

choices.label: Go once, leave by midnight
choices.desc: See what the fuss is about.

out.text: Loud, glamorous, slightly boring. He leaves at midnight and is in bed by one. Nothing happens. Nothing is good.
He leaves at midnight — but a photo from 11:58 looks like 3am. It's on a gossip account by morning.

choices.label: Become a regular
choices.text: The weekends blur. His touch in training gets heavier. {Mf} stops making eye contact. The people closest to him start asking questions.

choices.label: Say no
choices.text: He says no. He watches {SHOW} instead. On Monday, two teammates who went look exhausted.

scenarios.title: The Weekend Catches Up
text: Monday morning. {J}'s fitness test results are the worst in the squad. {Mf} pins them on the wall, without names, but everyone knows.
A gossip account has posted a video of {J} at 4am. The club's head of security forwards it to him with no message.

choices.label: Quit the scene completely
choices.text: He deletes the promoter's number. The first quiet Saturday feels like withdrawal. By the third, he sleeps through the night.

choices.label: Cut back, don't quit
choices.text: He tells himself he's in control. Some weeks, he is.

choices.label: Carry on
choices.text: He carries on. The papers carry on too. {Mf} drops him for the next match without explanation.

scenarios.title: The First Tattoo
text: Half the squad has tattoos. {J} has been thinking about one for months: something for his family, maybe. {MUM} has said, many times, 'over my dead body'.
{T} is getting a new tattoo on Thursday and has booked a second slot 'in case {J} grows a spine'.

choices.label: Family names on the forearm
choices.text: His family's names, in his father's handwriting, copied from an old birthday card. {MUM} cries when she sees it. She says it's because she's angry.

choices.label: Something wild
choices.text: It's enormous. The tiger looks slightly surprised. The fans love it. {MUM} doesn't speak to him for a week.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.text: He goes with {T} and watches. {T}'s tattoo is spelled wrong. {J} feels very wise.

scenarios.title: An Investment Opportunity
text: A smooth man in a smooth suit has an investment opportunity: crypto, real estate, 'guaranteed' returns. Three other players have already invested, he says.
{T} swears he doubled his money in six months with 'a guy'. The guy wants to meet {J}.

out.text: It actually works. His money grows. He becomes insufferable about it.
Six months later the smooth man's phone is disconnected. So is {J}'s money. Three other players are in the same position. None of them talk about it.

choices.label: Ask a real financial adviser
choices.text: The adviser laughs at the smooth man's brochure and builds {J} a boring, sensible plan. Boring is good.

choices.label: Walk away
choices.text: He walks away. A year later, a teammate tells him he lost everything to the same man.

scenarios.title: One More Game
text: It's 2:40am. {J} has been playing online since dinner. Training is at nine. He tells himself 'one more game' for the eleventh time.
{J}'s screen-time report says nine hours a day. The physio says his sleep data is 'concerning'.

choices.label: Put the console in a cupboard
choices.text: The first few nights are boring. Then he reads a book. Then he sleeps eight hours. His training numbers jump.

choices.label: Turn it into streaming
choices.text: The streams are popular. The sleep is not. His followers grow. His sprint times don't.

choices.label: It's fine, it's relaxing
choices.text: He keeps playing. His legs feel heavy in every Monday session.

scenarios.title: Starting a Foundation
text: {J}'s agent suggests starting a foundation: good for the image, good for the tax bill, good for the soul. In that order, says the agent.
{MUM} suggests {J} give something back to the neighbourhood. She already has a list. It's long.

choices.label: Yes, run it properly
choices.text: The foundation's first project builds a futsal court in his old neighbourhood. He's at the opening, crying, pretending it's the wind.

choices.label: Just donate quietly
choices.text: He donates {cost} anonymously. Nobody knows. That's the point.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.text: 'Later,' he says. {MUM} folds her list away and says nothing.

scenarios.title: Too Much Phone
text: {J}'s phone tells him he picked it up 247 times yesterday. He scrolled through his own mentions for three hours.
The club psychologist asks {J} to hand over his phone for the duration of the session. He feels physically anxious without it.

choices.label: Delete the apps for a month
choices.text: The first week is strange: hands reaching for a phone that's empty. By week three he's reading again. His mind feels like a room someone has cleaned.

choices.label: Hire a social media manager
choices.text: The posts become polished and slightly soulless. His mentions are someone else's problem now.

choices.label: It's fine
choices.text: He keeps scrolling. The bad comments keep finding him.

scenarios.title: Scratch on the New Car
text: Someone has keyed the new car. Deep, deliberate, the full length of it. In the club car park. CCTV shows a hooded figure.
{J} reverses the new car into a bollard outside {PLACE}. A crowd gathers. Phones come out.

choices.label: Laugh it off
choices.text: He posts a photo of the damage: 'At least it wasn't my hamstring.' The fans love it.

choices.label: Go after whoever did it
choices.text: Weeks of statements and calls. It turns out to be a fan of {R}. The story makes the papers.

scenarios.title: A House for {MUM} and {DAD}
text: For years {J} has dreamed of this: buying his parents a new house. He has the money now. He has the brochure. He has not asked them.
{MUM} mentions, casually, that the roof is leaking again. {J} looks at his bank account. Then at the photo of his parents on his phone.

out.text: He hands {MUM} the keys on video. She screams, then cries, then hits him for spending so much. {DAD} walks through every room twice and doesn't say a word until the garden, where he says 'good soil'.
{DAD} refuses to move. 'This is our home.' It takes three months of arguments before he agrees to a new roof instead.

choices.label: Ask them what they actually want
choices.text: They want to stay in the neighbourhood, with a new kitchen and a garden for {DAD}'s chillies. It costs a third of a new house and makes them happier.

scenarios.title: Back to the Books
text: A teammate is doing an online business degree in his spare time. He says every footballer should plan for 'life after'. {J} has never thought about life after.
The players' union offers free online courses: coaching, finance, languages, media.

choices.label: Coaching badges
choices.desc: Learn the game from the other side.
choices.text: The theory sessions change how he sees training. {Mf} starts asking his opinion.

choices.label: A language
choices.text: Twenty minutes a day. Six months later, he can order food and flirt, badly, in a new language.

choices.label: Too busy
choices.text: 'Later,' he says. It's what everyone says.

scenarios.title: Fashion Week
text: A fashion house invites {J} to sit in the front row of their show. Free clothes, free flights, a hotel with a doorman who wears gloves.
A designer wants {J} to walk in her show. Actually walk. On a runway. In front of people.

out.text: He walks like he's been doing it for years. Fashion magazines call him 'football's new face'. The squad calls him 'the model' forever.
He trips on the third step. The clip has fifty million views. The designer says it was 'intentional performance art'.

choices.label: Front row only
choices.text: He sits next to a pop star who has no idea who he is. The photos are everywhere anyway.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: He declines. The club's fitness coach is relieved. His {SIBr} is devastated.

scenarios.title: The Sleep Problem
text: {J} hasn't slept more than five hours a night in three weeks. The club's sports scientist shows him the data on a tablet. It's red.
Bags under his eyes, coffee at 4pm, staring at the ceiling at 2am. The body is talking. {J} isn't listening.

choices.label: Hire a sleep specialist
choices.text: Blackout blinds, a strict routine, no phone after nine. The first full night's sleep feels like a miracle.

choices.label: Talk to someone about what's keeping you up
choices.text: The club psychologist asks one question and {J} talks for an hour. The sleep starts coming back.

choices.label: More coffee
choices.text: Four coffees a day. His hands shake slightly in the warm-up.

scenarios.title: A Luxury Holiday
text: The off-season. The squad's group chat is full of yacht photos. A travel agent has sent {J} a brochure for a private island. It's very private. It's very expensive.
{T} has invited {J} on a holiday: private villa, chef, jet skis. 'Split it six ways, it's nothing.' It's not nothing.

choices.label: Go, enjoy every minute
choices.text: Ten days of sun and silence. He comes back tanned and calm. A paparazzi photo of him on a jet ski makes the papers.

choices.label: Take the family instead
choices.text: {MUM} has never seen the sea. She stands in it fully dressed for an hour. {DAD} falls asleep on a sunbed and gets a sunburn in the shape of his newspaper.

choices.label: Stay home, save the money
choices.text: He stays home. The yacht photos keep coming. He's fine with it. Mostly.

scenarios.title: A YouTube Channel
text: A production company wants to launch a vlog channel with {J}: behind-the-scenes, daily life, pranks. They'll handle everything. They want 30% of the revenue and access to his whole life.
{SIB} has started filming {J} for TikTok without asking. The videos are doing better than his actual account.

choices.label: Launch a full vlog
choices.text: The first video gets a million views. The cameras follow him everywhere. The people closest to him start to hate the red recording light.

choices.label: Let {SIB} run a small channel
choices.text: {SIB}'s videos are shaky, unfiltered and wildly popular. {SIB} is now more famous than most of the squad.

choices.label: No cameras
choices.text: He says no. His life stays his own.

scenarios.title: Finding a Place to Pray
text: In a new country, {J} hasn't found a place to pray, or a community. Sunday or Friday comes and goes and feels empty.
A teammate notices {J} praying alone in the physio room before matches. He mentions there's a community centre across town.

choices.label: Go and introduce yourself
choices.text: The community welcomes him like a son. An old man invites him to dinner. For an evening, he's not a footballer. He's just someone's guest.

choices.label: Keep it private
choices.text: He keeps his rituals to himself. They anchor him, even alone.

scenarios.title: The Card Game
text: On the team bus, a card game for money has been going for months. The stakes have crept up. Tonight a teammate lost a month's wages in an hour.
A teammate invites {J} to a 'private poker night'. The address is a penthouse. The buy-in is a number with a lot of zeros.

out.text: He loses a little, laughs, leaves. That's it.
He wins. Big. It's the worst thing that could have happened. He wants to play again.

choices.label: Never play
choices.text: He reads on the bus instead. Six months later, two teammates owe money to people they shouldn't.

scenarios.title: Chasing Losses
text: {J} has been betting online. Small at first. Then less small. Last night he lost more than a month's wages and tried to win it back. Then he lost more.
The betting app sends {J} a notification: 'We miss you! Here's a free bet.' He opens it at 3am.

choices.label: Ask for help
choices.text: The welfare officer has seen this a hundred times. She doesn't judge. The road out starts with blocking the apps.

ok.text: He deletes everything and changes his bank settings. It's hard. He does it.

bad.text: He lasts nine days. Then the free bet arrives.

choices.label: One more big win and you'll stop
choices.text: He doesn't win it back. He loses {cost} more. The bank calls. So does {DAD}.

scenarios.title: Less Is More
text: A veteran teammate lives in a simple apartment, drives an old car and has saved enough to never work again. 'Nobody remembers your watch,' he says.
{J} looks around his apartment at things he bought and never used: a massage chair, three games consoles, a coffee machine with a manual like a novel.

choices.label: Simplify everything
choices.text: He sells half of everything and gives the rest away. His living costs drop. Strangely, he feels lighter.

choices.label: Keep living well
choices.text: He keeps the massage chair. He uses it. It's great.

scenarios.title: Security
text: Fans followed {J} home last night. Three of them. Friendly, but they now know where he lives. The club's head of security suggests a bodyguard.
Someone has posted {J}'s apartment building online. A small crowd gathers outside every evening.

choices.label: Hire a bodyguard
choices.text: His bodyguard is huge and silent and very good at chess. Fans can't get close anymore. Some say he's 'changed'.

choices.label: Move somewhere private
choices.text: A gated house outside the city. Safe. Quiet. Very far from the world he came from.

choices.label: Talk to the fans
choices.text: He goes down, signs everything, and asks them nicely to give him privacy. Most of them do.

scenarios.title: Learning to Cook
text: {J}'s fridge contains: protein shakes, three eggs, and a jar of something {MUM} sent that he's afraid to open. The nutritionist has had enough. She's booked him a cooking class.
{J} has eaten the same chicken and rice for 41 days. A teammate's wife runs cooking classes. She has offered.

choices.label: Go every week
choices.hint: Healthier. Happier. Better at dinner parties.
choices.text: By week six he can make three dishes properly. He cooks for {T} and his family. Everyone survives.

choices.label: Hire a private chef
choices.text: The chef is excellent and costs {cost} a month. {J}'s fridge is now beautiful and he still can't boil an egg.

scenarios.title: Back in the Old Neighbourhood
text: {J} drives through the neighbourhood where he grew up. The street vendors, the broken goalpost, the wall where he used to kick a ball for hours. Everyone stops what they're doing.
A visit home. The kids who used to call him names now ask for selfies.

choices.label: Walk the whole street
choices.text: Three hours, a hundred handshakes, eight plates of food he couldn't refuse. The old woman who sold him ice lollies when he was six cries.

choices.label: Fix the broken goalpost
choices.text: A new goal, new nets, a small sign with no name on it. The kids know who did it.
